case_name: State of Maharashtra v Sadruddin Jan Mohommad Bardia and Others
facts: The State of Maharashtra has preferred this appeal challenging the judgment of the High Court of Bombay (Nagpur Bench) made in Criminal Appeal No. 206 of 1974 dated January 16, 1979.
Admittedly the main accused Nasrulla who is said to have been benefited by this transaction is still absconding.
The offence complained of is said to have been committed in the year 1974.
respondent_arguments: Giving the benefit of doubt to the respondents acquitted both of them.
court_reasoning: Applying the said principle to the facts of the present case, it we look for any line between the commission of the offence of cheating the Central Bank of India by Nasrulla and the making out of the receipts Exts. 15, 17 and 19 by accused Nos. 1 and 2, it must be held that the prosecution has failed to establish that link.

Similarly, there is no evidence and the link between the making of the MTRs and delivery of the MTRs or their ultimate finding their way in the hands of Nasrulla has also not been established by the prosecution beyond a reasonable doubt.
cases_cited: State of Maharashtra v Sadruddin Jan Mohommad Bardia
